docs.title: Scope clue
docs.text: No cross-tenant reuse occurred. The disclosure crossed principals and policy epochs inside one tenant. The security invariant covers both.

docs.title: 1. Build a causal graph
docs.text:
Connect release, cache identity, bypassed stages, stale authority, prose disclosure, denied citation, and misleading green metrics.

[change] --> [boundary bypass] --> [unauthorized bytes/claim] --> [user harm]
                   |                         |
                   +--> [missing signal] <---+

docs.title: 2. Rank hypotheses
docs.text: Hypothesis Evidence for Evidence against Test Rank Model fabricated target ACL event was delayed Vector index retained stale chunk Answer cache reused across authority scopes Tenant router crossed tenant boundary

docs.title: 3. Choose immediate actions
docs.text: Order actions for affected tenant quarantine, regional/global cache kill, payload purge, version rollback, token/session action, audit preservation, customer notification, and broader exposure search. Explain which action reduces disclosure fastest and which preserves evidence.

docs.title: 4. Attribute detection failure
docs.text: Explain why retrieval canaries, queue lag, and sampled support quality stayed green. Define the missing numerator, denominator, dimensions, and synthetic test.

docs.title: 5. Define repair and exit criteria
docs.text: Specify cache authority semantics, reauthorization behavior during dependency failure, cache invalidation, old payload purge, regression datasets, rollout cohort, and conditions for restoring cache traffic.

docs.title: Facilitator diagnosis
docs.text:
Open after completing the diagnosis

The primary cause is an authorization bypass in 4.18.0: answer text was cached at tenant scope and returned before current per-principal authorization of its evidence. Citation authorization protected the link but not the prose. The supplied source event reached the deny map in 12 seconds, but the end-to-end non-disclosure SLO was violated by the cache path. Healthy component propagation is not an end-to-end SLO pass.

u-923 authorized at epoch 771
          |
          v
  [tenant-only cache entry]
          |
          | key omits principal/scope, generation, evidence versions
          v
u-184 epoch 772 ----X----> full retrieval/hydration authorization
          |
          +-------------> cached board conclusion disclosed
                                   |
                                   +--> citation resolver denies only the link

Contributors:

  1. Threat modeling treated summaries as non-sensitive even though they preserve facts.
  2. Cache-hit SLI had no authorization decision or evidence recheck count.
  3. Isolation canaries tested cross-tenant boundaries but not cross-principal revocation.
  4. Supported-answer sampling measured entailment, not caller authorization.
  5. A feature flag controlled lookup but rollback did not purge stored payloads.

Not primary: model hallucination, delayed source event, vector stale data, or tenant routing. They remain plausible in other incidents and should be tested rather than dismissed.

docs.title: Reference containment order
docs.text:
1. Disable answer-cache reads globally or in the affected region; preserve metadata snapshots under incident access controls.
  2. Quarantine affected tenant if reproduction persists; force full authorized path.
  3. Purge cache payloads by incompatible schema/version, including replicas.
  4. Enumerate 4.18.0 cache-hit runs, re-evaluate cited versions against then-current and current policy, and notify Security/Privacy incident owners.
  5. Keep citation rendering fail closed and revoke derived conversation summaries that copied affected text.
  6. Roll back code, then verify no legacy reader can consume old entries.

Do not "fix" by placing principal ID alone in the key. Group membership, explicit denies, policy epochs, source versions, legal purpose, residency, and cache lifetime can change. A safe design either reauthorizes all evidence on every hit or uses a capability/scope fingerprint with bounded age plus current deny checks; denial or policy-service uncertainty fails closed.

docs.title: Exit criteria
docs.text:
• Zero unauthorized disclosures across cross-tenant, cross-principal, revoked-group, explicit-deny, and policy-epoch race suites.
  • Every cache hit records a current authorization decision for every evidence version before prose release.
  • Incompatible payload count is zero across primary, replica, and edge caches.
  • Revocation p99 remains below 60 seconds under cache-hit load and entitlement degradation.
  • Security completes exposure analysis; Privacy decides notifications and evidence retention.
  • Canary progresses 1%, 5%, 25%, 50%, 100% with an automatic leak-count kill switch and named release commander.

docs.title: Prevention review
docs.text: Add answer caches, summaries, logs, traces, replay stores, and conversation memory to the data-flow threat model. Gate optimization releases on authorization-preserving equivalence, not only latency. Make cache_hit_without_current_auth > 0 an invariant alarm. Maintain planted per-principal and per-tenant secrets whose appearance anywhere outside authorized runs pages Security.

docs.title: Progressive Hints
docs.text:
Practice home | Prompt | Workbook

Open one level at a time. Each level spends interview signal. The first hints frame questions; later hints disclose increasingly concrete mechanisms.

Hint 1: Separate truth, permission, and generated prose

List who owns source bytes, source version, group membership, access decision, searchable representation, and final answer. A model cannot be authoritative for any of them.

Checkpoint: Can the system explain why this principal could see this span at this time?

Hint 2: Trace the negative case

Start with a question for which useful text exists but none is authorized. The correct outcome must not reveal titles, counts, snippets, timing distinctions, or suggested queries derived from hidden material.

Checkpoint: Does no-answer look materially different when a hidden match exists?

Hint 3: Authorization is not a final decoration

Ask where candidates are generated, where full text is hydrated, where context is packed, and where citations are opened. Carry immutable tenant scope and a policy version through the path. Recheck current authorization before text enters model context and before a citation is rendered.

Checkpoint: Can stale index metadata alone disclose revoked text?

Hint 4: Preserve the evidence chain

A useful searchable unit can carry tenant, source ID, immutable source version, span offsets, digest, ACL or security-domain reference, residency, parser version, and index generation. The answer can map each material claim to those units.

Checkpoint: Does a citation silently point at new text after the source changes?

Hint 5: Retrieval stages solve different errors

Lexical search protects exact names, codes, and rare terms. Vector search broadens semantic recall. Rank fusion avoids comparing unrelated score scales directly. A reranker improves ordering over a bounded authorized set. Context packing enforces diversity, token, trust, and version constraints.

Checkpoint: Can you measure candidate recall separately from answer support?

Hint 6: Make abstention testable

Define answerable, unanswerable, contradictory, stale, and unauthorized cases. Measure retrieval recall, ranking quality, claim-level citation precision/recall, supported-answer rate, no-answer precision/recall, leakage, latency, and cost by tenant and language slice.

Checkpoint: Is a fluent unsupported answer counted as success anywhere?

Hint 7: Revocation needs a fast deny path

Index cleanup may take longer than the disclosure SLO. Consider a monotonically ordered change record, a current authorization check, and a deny/tombstone mechanism that becomes effective before physical index removal. Measure with synthetic canaries from source acceptance to failed retrieval and cache eviction.

Checkpoint: What fails closed during an identity or policy outage?

Hint 8: Quantify the derived corpus

Fifty million documents at 12 chunks each yields 600 million chunks. For 1,024-dimensional float16 vectors, raw vectors alone are about 600M * 1,024 * 2 = 1.2288 TB decimal before graph, lexical index, metadata, replicas, headroom, and a second migration generation.

Checkpoint: Can the platform hold two complete generations without stealing failure headroom?

Hint 9: Isolation is a property of every plane

Threat-model routing, index namespaces, caches, queues, object keys, logs, traces, evaluation exports, model-provider requests, support tooling, deletion jobs, and backup restore. Use tenant-bound identities and reject scope mismatches; never fall back to an unscoped global search.

Checkpoint: Which automated test plants a unique canary and proves it cannot cross a tenant boundary?

Hint 10: Migration changes two coupled variables

Changing embeddings without changing chunks is easier to compare than changing embedding, chunking, and ranker together. Build a versioned generation, backfill from immutable source versions, consume a change log, shadow reads, compare safety and quality, canary by tenant, then move an atomic routing manifest. Keep the old generation current until rollback expires.

Checkpoint: What happens to an update that arrives between backfill and cutover?

Hint 11: Region is part of identity

Bind tenant to an approved residency policy and route ingestion, indexes, query text, context, model invocation, caches, replay records, and evaluation artifacts accordingly. A global control plane can retain minimal non-content metadata, but failover must not silently move restricted data.

Checkpoint: Is an unavailable compliant region allowed to fail over to a prohibited one?

Hint 12: L6 evidence

Connect architecture to measurable gates, value at risk, ownership, incident authority, migration capacity, rollout cohorts, rollback semantics, audit evidence, and reversal conditions. Explain how search, identity, source-integrations, ML, security, privacy, and regional operations teams share contracts without sharing ambiguity.

Checkpoint: Could those teams ship and operate the change without relying on the designer's memory?

After the timer, continue to the evidence rubric.

docs.title: Interviewer Packet
docs.text:
Practice home | Rubric | Exemplars

This file contains answer-bearing disclosures and probes. Keep it closed until the candidate's first pass is complete.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Assess whether the candidate can deliver useful retrieval without allowing generated behavior, stale indexes, caches, or regional failover to exceed a principal's current authority. Reward a coherent safe path over a catalog of AI products.

docs.title: Mode selection
docs.text: Mode Core evidence Optional branch 15 minutes Boundaries, invariants, question contract, answer/no-answer, revocation race Citation mutation 30 minutes Safe core plus records/events, hybrid retrieval, deletion, evaluation, telemetry Group expansion 45 minutes Full core plus capacity, skew, threat model, regions, failure attribution Model outage 60 minutes Full design plus zero-downtime migration, rollout, ownership, reversal Adversarial review

docs.title: Opening script
docs.text:
Design a read-only enterprise knowledge assistant over 50 million documents and 20,000 tenants. Answers require citations and must respect current permission and residency. Start with scope and correctness invariants. Narrate authority, versions, and failure behavior as you draw.

Do not suggest ACL-prefiltering, hybrid retrieval, reranking, tombstones, or dual indexes. Let the candidate discover the mechanisms.

docs.title: Facts available only on request
docs.text: Candidate asks about Disclosure Signal to observe Identity OIDC authenticates users. An entitlement service resolves nested groups and returns a signed, tenant-bound policy snapshot with an epoch. Does not trust claims copied from a client token forever ACL semantics Sources support user/group allows, explicit denies, inheritance, and tenant-approved cross-project sharing; deny wins. Establishes one normalized policy contract Source events Connectors provide a cursor but can duplicate, reorder, omit, and later repair events. Nightly source enumeration is available. Combines ordered application with anti-entropy Content versions Most sources expose immutable revision IDs; object storage versions require the connector to compute a content digest. Preserves citation identity Query mix 35% exact identifiers/names, 45% conceptual questions, 20% mixed. Four languages account for 95%. Justifies retrieval stages and slices Answer policy No answer is preferable to an unsupported answer. A qualification is acceptable when sources conflict and both are cited. Defines thresholds and user semantics Deletion Contract clock begins when the authoritative source accepts deletion or permission revocation, not when a connector notices it. Identifies source-to-serving measurement Caches Product wants semantic and answer caching, but correctness overrides hit rate. Keys and reauthorizes by tenant/policy/evidence generation Residency Tenants choose EU, US, or APAC. EU content and derived data may use only approved EU facilities; outages may reduce availability. Fails compliant rather than crossing region Model provider Regional endpoints exist. Provider contract disables training and has zero payload retention, but platform must still minimize sent text. Treats contract as one control, not the whole boundary Scale Average 12 chunks/document, 1,024-dimensional current embeddings, RF=2 inside a region. Performs derived capacity math Evaluation Product has thumbs-up logs but no curated benchmark. Builds versioned labels rather than treating clicks as truth Existing index Current lexical index is authoritative for search and supports current ACL filtering; migration introduces vector retrieval. Preserves safe authority during migration

docs.title: Minute 5
docs.text:
Look for authorities and non-disclosure. If absent:

Which facts may be stale, and which may never be stale at disclosure time?

docs.title: Minute 15
docs.text:
Look for an authorized query trace, immutable evidence, and no-answer. If absent:

A useful paragraph exists but the user lost group membership 20 seconds ago. Trace it.

docs.title: Minute 30
docs.text:
Look for end-to-end deletion measurement and evaluation decomposition. If absent:

Queue lag is zero but a deletion canary still appears. Where can the old bytes survive?

docs.title: Minute 45
docs.text:
Look for workload arithmetic, tenant skew, regional behavior, and attribution. Ask:

Supported-answer rate fell three points after a release. What retained evidence identifies the responsible stage?

docs.title: Minute 55
docs.text:
Look for generation migration, gates, rollback freshness, and owners. Ask:

Shadow quality is better overall but two small-language tenants regress and migration storage has 12% headroom. Who may cut over?

docs.title: Branching follow-ups
docs.text: Choose the branch nearest the candidate's current design. Do not exhaust the list.

docs.title: Branch A: Global vector search then filtering
docs.text:
1. Does the ANN service observe hidden vectors, tenant size, scores, or timing?
  2. What happens when authorized matches are crowded out of top K by inaccessible matches?
  3. Can an empty-result timing oracle reveal a document's existence?
  4. What physical or cryptographic boundary narrows the candidate universe?

Strong evidence: tenant/security-domain routing before candidate generation, mandatory server-side filters within that boundary, current authorization before hydration, and negative isolation tests.

docs.title: Branch B: Authorization is strong
docs.text:
1. Nested group expansion is unavailable. Which requests proceed?
  2. Membership changes after retrieval but before streaming token 500. What happens?
  3. A shared document changes from project A to project B while old chunks remain.
  4. How can support investigate without bypassing tenant policy?

Strong evidence: bounded signed snapshots, fail-closed freshness rules, pre-context reauthorization, stream cancellation or policy binding, tombstones, and audited break-glass with customer-visible governance.

docs.title: Branch C: Retrieval is strong
docs.text:
1. How do you fuse incomparable BM25 and cosine scores?
  2. Which metric identifies loss before reranking?
  3. The reranker times out. What safe quality mode remains?
  4. How do duplicate chunks from two revisions avoid crowding context?

Strong evidence: rank-based or calibrated fusion, recall@K and NDCG separation, bounded fallback, version-aware dedupe, diversity, and token budgets.

docs.title: Branch D: Candidate says citations prevent hallucinations
docs.text:
1. A citation is relevant to the topic but not to the attached claim. Is it valid?
  2. A sentence combines two claims supported by different spans.
  3. The title is visible but opening the span is now denied.
  4. How are citation labels produced and audited?

Strong evidence: claim-span entailment/support labels, citation precision and recall, immutable versions, current render authorization, and no hidden metadata in denial.

docs.title: Branch E: Candidate relies on full reindex for deletion
docs.text:
1. Can 600 million chunks be rebuilt inside 60 seconds?
  2. What about answer caches, replicas, reranker caches, and replay records?
  3. How is a missed source event found?
  4. What proves a tenant's deletion met its contract?

Strong evidence: immediate policy/tombstone denial, versioned cache dependencies, asynchronous physical purge, anti-entropy, synthetic canaries, and an erasure evidence ledger.

docs.title: Branch F: Multi-region active-active
docs.text:
1. EU is unavailable. May its query context go to the US?
  2. Two regions see different group epochs. Which can answer?
  3. How is tenant routing changed without split-brain ingestion?
  4. Which metadata is safe in a global control plane?

Strong evidence: residency-pinned data plane, fail-closed restricted failover, single regional ingestion ownership or fenced leases, minimal global metadata, and audited routing epochs.

docs.title: Branch G: Candidate proposes dual index migration
docs.text:
1. Which immutable snapshot seeds the new generation?
  2. How are concurrent updates replayed and gaps detected?
  3. Can a tenant query generations with different permission semantics?
  4. What remains current during rollback, and when may old data be deleted?

Strong evidence: snapshot watermark plus CDC, idempotent version application, parity and isolation gates, tenant-atomic routing, old-generation catch-up, and rollback expiry.

docs.title: Branch H: Operationally strong candidate
docs.text:
1. Which alarm pages Security rather than Search?
  2. How do metrics preserve tenant isolation and bounded cardinality?
  3. What is the first containment for one suspected cross-tenant citation?
  4. How do you distinguish a source outage from an embedding outage?

Strong evidence: global kill/tenant quarantine, audit preservation, stage-specific SLIs and versioned traces, synthetic canaries, incident roles, and conservative re-enable criteria.

docs.title: Reference architecture for calibration
docs.text:
This is one valid shape, not a required component list.

                         GLOBAL CONTROL (metadata only)
       tenant -> region | generation manifest | policy schema versions
                              | signed routing epoch
              +---------------+----------------+
              v                                v
     +---------------- EU DATA PLANE ----------------+
     |                                               |
user |  authn -> entitlement/policy -> query broker  |
---->|                   |              |            |
     |                   |scope         +--> lexical |
     |                   |              +--> vector  |
     |                   |                   |        |
     |                   +-----------> rank fusion    |
     |                                      |         |
     |        current policy recheck <--- hydrate     |
     |                                      |         |
     |    authorized rerank -> context/model           |
     |          citation map <--- model output         |
     |                |                     |         |
<----| answer/no-answer + final citation authorization|
     |                                               |
     | source -> connector -> version log -> builders |
     |                  |          |          |       |
     |                  +----> deny/tombstone  indexes|
     +-----------------------------------------------+

No content/context arrow crosses the regional box.

flowchart LR
    U[Authenticated principal] --> G[Regional query gateway]
    G --> P[Entitlement and policy]
    G --> B[Retrieval broker]
    P --> B
    B --> L[(Tenant-scoped lexical)]
    B --> V[(Tenant-scoped vectors)]
    L --> F[Rank fusion]
    V --> F
    F --> H[Current authorization and hydration]
    H --> R[Authorized text reranking]
    R --> M[Regional model]
    M --> C[Claim and citation verifier]
    P --> C
    C --> U

Suggested records:

TenantRoute(tenant_id, residency_policy, data_region, routing_epoch)
SourceVersion(tenant_id, source_id, version, digest, uri, observed_at, source_commit_at)
PolicyObject(tenant_id, object_id, policy_version, allow_refs, deny_refs, inheritance, region)
Chunk(chunk_id, source_id, source_version, offsets, digest, parser_version)
IndexManifest(tenant_id, generation, lexical_version, embedding_version, state, watermark)
DeletionIntent(tenant_id, object_id, source_commit_at, seq, state, purge_deadline)
Run(run_id, tenant_id, principal_ref, policy_epoch, region, query_digest, versions, status)
Retrieval(run_id, stage, candidate_ids, ranks, scores, authorization_decision_refs)
Answer(run_id, disposition, claim_spans, citation_ids, model_version, prompt_version)

Suggested question API:

POST /v1/tenants/{tenant}/questions
Authorization: Bearer <principal credential>
Idempotency-Key: <request retry identity>

{"question":"...","conversation_ref":"...","max_wait_ms":8000}

200 {"disposition":"ANSWERED|QUALIFIED|NO_ANSWER","answer":"...",
     "citations":[{"claim_ids":["c1"],"source_id":"...","source_version":"...",
                   "start":120,"end":244,"digest":"..."}],
     "evidence_as_of":"...","run_id":"..."}

The server derives tenant authorization from authenticated routing, not the path alone. A retry may replay the stored result only after current authorization of every cited version; otherwise it recomputes or returns no answer.

Use 400 for invalid bounded input, 401/403 for authentication/tenant access without revealing resource existence, 409 POLICY_CHANGED before response headers when a stream or replay cannot safely start under the required epoch, 429 with a retry hint for admission control, and 503 when current authorization or the compliant region is unavailable. NO_ANSWER is a successful product result, not a transport error. Once a stream has started, its HTTP status cannot change to 409: emit a defined terminal policy-change event and stop further output. Already delivered text cannot be retracted, so the streaming contract must specify the authorization freshness bound and recheck/cancellation behavior.

One valid materialization lifecycle is:

DISCOVERED -> BUILDING -> ACTIVE -> SUPERSEDED -> PURGE_PENDING -> PURGED
                    |          |             |
                    +----------+----deny-----+

An ACL revoke can make any non-purged state non-retrievable immediately.
An older object sequence cannot move PURGE_PENDING or PURGED back to ACTIVE.

docs.title: Capacity anchor
docs.text:
Accept alternatives with explicit assumptions.

chunks                         = 50M * 12 = 600M
raw float16 vectors            = 600M * 1,024 * 2 B = 1.2288 TB
assumed ANN graph + IDs        = 600M * 576 B = 345.6 GB
assumed lexical/metadata       = 600M * 1.5 KB = 900 GB
one generation                = 2.4744 TB decimal
RF=2 with 30% of capacity free = 2.4744 * 2 / 0.70 = 7.07 TB
two generations during change = 14.14 TB before snapshots/build scratch

average changes/s              = 5M / 86,400 = 57.9
20x burst                      = 1,157 changes/s
if 12 chunks and 2 indexes     = 27,768 chunk-index mutations/s at burst
six-hour outage backlog        = 57.9 * 21,600 = 1.25M source changes average

peak vector candidates         = 6,000 * 120 = 720K/s
peak lexical candidates        = 6,000 * 120 = 720K/s
reranker at 40/query           = 240K pairs/s
8 chunks * 600 tokens + 1,200 other = 6,000 input tokens/query
peak model input               = 36M tokens/s before cache or admission

Numbers show why quotas, batching, tiering, and explicit model capacity are required. They are not benchmark claims.

Sensitivity: if richer parsing doubles the average to 24 chunks/document, index storage, backfill work, and mutation fan-out roughly double; dual-generation allocation rises from about 14.14 TB to 28.28 TB under the same assumptions. A 30% uplift on demand (*1.3) leaves only 0.3/1.3 = 23.08% of provisioned capacity free; it does not meet a 30%-free gate. Reserve regional capacity before enabling the parser or use measured compression/tiering rather than consume incident headroom.

docs.title: Evaluation anchor
docs.text:
Require source-span labels and authorized principal snapshots. A credible release suite includes answerable, unanswerable, contradictory, revoked, deleted, cross-tenant canary, exact identifier, multilingual, long-document, stale-source, and prompt-injected slices.

Core metrics: recall@K, MRR or NDCG@K, authorization precision (must be 1.0 in tested cases), cross-tenant leakage count (must be zero), claim support precision/recall, citation precision/recall, supported-answer rate, no-answer precision/recall, freshness and revocation latency distributions, p95/p99 latency, tokens, and cost. Report slices and confidence intervals; aggregate gains cannot waive a safety regression.

docs.title: Evidence notes and calibration
docs.text:
Capture exact candidate statements and whether independently offered or prompted. Apply the rubric, including mode normalization and caps.

Topic Positive evidence Risk evidence Authority / invariants API / lifecycle Permission / isolation Retrieval / citations Capacity / latency Freshness / deletion Evaluation / attribution Threats / residency Operations Migration / leadership

Strong L5: independently makes the bounded regional service safe, measurable, and implementable, including current authorization, evidence/no-answer, deletion, and incident behavior.

Strong L6: additionally shapes policy contracts across teams, quantifies migration and operational risk, establishes decision rights, and makes generation and regional evolution reversible.

docs.title: Debrief script
docs.text:
1. Cite one exact decision that protected users or evidence quality.
  2. Describe the highest-risk concrete failure sequence.
  3. State the normalized mode score and any cap.
  4. Name the artifact or experiment needed for the next level.

Do not award points for "vector database," "zero trust," "hybrid," or "LLM guardrail" without a boundary and test. Do not penalize safe regional partitioning or no-answer as reduced availability. Do not reveal the reference design during the interview.

A correct no-answer is a successful product outcome; a fail-closed 503 still consumes the availability error budget even when it is the safest decision. Evaluate the safety of that tradeoff without redefining availability. A 60-second propagation SLO is also not instantaneous revocation: state the allowed stale interval and fail-closed behavior when no sufficiently fresh authorization view can be established.

docs.title: Migration Exercise: Zero-Downtime Embedding and Index Evolution
docs.text: Practice home | Rubric | Interviewer packet

docs.title: Starting system
docs.text:
Generation G1 serves all tenants from a regional lexical index plus a 1,024-dimensional embedding index. It uses chunker C3, embedding E4, ACL schema P6, reranker R2, and citation schema S3. The source-version log is durable, but the original rollout used mutable aliases and coarse progress counters.

The proposed G2 introduces embedding E5, ANN engine V2, and quantization. Product also wants chunker C4. EU data must remain in EU. Queries cannot be paused. Revocations and deletions must meet existing SLOs throughout migration.

docs.title: Candidate task
docs.text: Design the migration control plane and rollout with zero query downtime. Address snapshot consistency, concurrent changes, capacity, compatibility, shadow evaluation, tenant-atomic cutover, rollback, deletion, regional execution, ownership, and retirement. Decide whether chunking changes in the same release.

docs.title: Migration invariants
docs.text:
1. A query uses one compatible generation manifest; no accidental mix of chunk, embedding, policy, ranker, or citation schema.
  2. Neither generation can broaden tenant or principal authority.
  3. Every source version, ACL change, revocation, and deletion after the seed watermark reaches each live or rollback-eligible generation.
  4. Routing changes atomically per tenant and is monotonic by routing epoch.
  5. Rollback never depends on a stale old generation.
  6. Restricted data and build artifacts remain in their approved region.
  7. Retirement cannot erase legal-hold evidence or retain deletable data beyond policy.

docs.title: Capacity gate
docs.text:
Using the pack assumptions:

G1 allocation with RF=2 and 30% capacity free      ~= 7.07 TB
G2 allocation with RF=2 and 30% capacity free      ~= 7.07 TB
temporary snapshots/build spill, 20% of G1 allocation ~= 1.41 TB
minimum migration allocation                         ~= 15.55 TB

5M changes/day * 7-day rollback window               = 35M change records
if one compact event averages 2 KB                    = 70 GB before RF/overhead
backfill target over 14 days                           = 600M / 1,209,600 s ~= 496 chunks/s
live update work, if every change rewrites 12 chunks    = 5M * 12 / 86,400 ~= 694 chunks/s
combined mean work for G2                              ~= 1,190 chunks/s
with a 2x total-work planning allowance                ~= 2,381 chunks/s

These are planning numbers, not vendor benchmarks. Migration does not start unless each region preserves normal failure headroom after dual-generation and build scratch allocation.

The live-work assumption is deliberately conservative: ACL-only changes and deletes need not re-embed content, but they still consume indexing/deny capacity. Measure change-class fractions and both generations' write paths. At a 20x source burst, 12-chunk rewrites alone demand about 13,889 chunks/s; the combined mean with a 2x allowance is not a burst guarantee. Preserve a separate priority path for revocations. Retain the change log from the initial snapshot through build, catch-up, rollback and safety lag, not merely the seven-day rollback interval.

docs.title: Required control-plane records
docs.text:
GenerationManifest(
  generation_id, region, chunker, embedding, vector_schema, lexical_schema,
  policy_schema, reranker_compatibility, citation_schema, build_watermark,
  state, created_at, digest
)

TenantRoute(tenant_id, generation_id, routing_epoch, changed_at, approver)
ObjectMaterialization(tenant_id, object_id, source_version, acl_seq, delete_seq,
                      acl_version, acl_digest, generation_id, content_digest,
                      state, applied_at)
BackfillPartition(generation_id, partition, snapshot_watermark, cursor, checksum, state)
ParityReport(generation_id, tenant_id, object_count, version_mismatch,
             acl_mismatch, tombstone_mismatch, sampled_digest_mismatch)

docs.title: Event contract
docs.text:
{
  "event_id": "stable-source-event-id",
  "tenant_id": "t-7",
  "object_id": "doc-91",
  "source_version": "v45",
  "object_sequence": 8842,
  "change": "UPSERT|ACL_CHANGE|DELETE",
  "acl_version": "acl-v119",
  "acl_ref": "source-acl://t-7/doc-91/acl-v119",
  "acl_digest": "sha256:...",
  "source_committed_at": "2026-08-17T09:07:00Z",
  "residency_policy": "EU",
  "content_digest": "sha256:..."
}

acl_ref resolves an immutable, versioned policy object; consumers verify acl_digest and never fetch an unversioned "current ACL" for a historical sequence. Materializers reject tenant/region mismatch, apply each object sequence idempotently, retain gap state, and reconcile gaps against source inventory. Deletes and denies fan out to every non-retired generation, including BUILDING, CATCHING_UP, SHADOW, CANARY, SERVING, ROLLBACK_READY, and QUARANTINED. A generation cannot advance state until its ACL/tombstone gaps and deletion parity are clean.

docs.title: Reference migration shape
docs.text: Open after drafting: migration stages, gates, and rollback

docs.title: Stage 0: Freeze contracts and baseline
docs.text:
• Record G1 manifest and stop mutable alias changes.
  • Version an evaluation set and seven days of privacy-approved replay features.
  • Measure supported-answer rate, no-answer, citation support, safety slices, p99, cost, revocation/deletion latency, index parity, and per-tenant skew.
  • Inventory capacity, consumers, caches, snapshots, backup retention, and team decision rights.

Gate: reproducible baseline, complete owner matrix, enough capacity, and proven emergency routing rollback.

docs.title: Stage 1: Decouple variables
docs.text:
Run E5/V2 on C3 first. Changing chunker and embedding together obscures attribution and invalidates span comparisons. Treat C4 as a later G3 unless a mandatory compatibility reason outweighs that diagnostic cost.

Gate: manifest compatibility validation rejects mixed schema combinations.

docs.title: Stage 2: Seed at watermark W
docs.text:
Create a region-local immutable source/ACL snapshot at log watermark W. Backfill deterministic partitions into G2; store per-object version, ACL sequence, deletion sequence, and digest. Builders use tenant-bound credentials and cannot write another region.

Gate: partition checksums, count reconciliation, no region violations, and no unexplained object/ACL/tombstone mismatch.

docs.title: Stage 3: Catch up concurrent changes
docs.text:
Consume events after W into both generations. Per-object sequences make replay idempotent and expose gaps. Compare source version and ACL/tombstone state, not only total document counts. Reserve queue capacity for revocations ahead of ordinary content updates.

 snapshot <= W ----backfill----+
                              +--> G2 parity barrier --> shadow eligible
 change log > W ----replay-----+

 live events --------------------> G1 (serving and rollback-current)
             +------------------> G2

Gate: lag below 10-minute freshness budget, revocation probes below 60 seconds, zero unresolved sequence gaps, and per-tenant parity thresholds.

docs.title: Stage 4: Shadow safely
docs.text:
For fixed labels and privacy-approved sampled production queries, execute G2 retrieval without exposing results. Reuse the caller's actual authorization scope; never broaden a shadow query for analysis. Store IDs/scores under regional retention controls, not raw unrestricted context.

Compare candidate recall@K, NDCG, exact-identifier recall, claim-support potential, empty authorized result, policy decision parity, latency, resource cost, language, tenant-size, and source-type slices.

Gate: zero unauthorized or cross-tenant candidates; 100% revocation/deletion canary compliance; no safety-slice regression; agreed quality gain; p99 under budget; at least 30% serving and sync headroom.

docs.title: Stage 5: Tenant-atomic canary
docs.text:
Move internal tenants, then 1%, 5%, 25%, 50%, and 100% using a signed TenantRoute compare-and-swap on routing epoch. All queries for one run resolve one manifest. Cohorts include large, small, multilingual, high-change, and regulated tenants; no cohort contains only easy traffic.

Automatic abort: any isolation leak, revocation SLO breach, residency violation, unexplained parity gap, p99 over 8 seconds for two windows, or capacity below 20%. Quality regressions pause promotion for review rather than silently averaging away a slice.

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> BUILDING
    BUILDING --> CATCHING_UP: snapshot complete
    CATCHING_UP --> SHADOW: parity barrier passes
    SHADOW --> CANARY: safety and quality gates pass
    CANARY --> SERVING: cohorts complete
    CANARY --> QUARANTINED: abort and route to known-good generation
    SERVING --> ROLLBACK_READY: replaced but kept current
    SERVING --> QUARANTINED: safety violation
    ROLLBACK_READY --> RETIRED: expiry and sign-off
    SHADOW --> QUARANTINED: safety violation
    CANARY --> QUARANTINED: safety violation

The diagram describes one generation. A failed candidate is quarantined; it does not become a rollback target merely because its rollout was aborted. ROLLBACK_READY applies to the previously validated generation that has been replaced and is still consuming changes.

docs.title: Stage 6: Roll back without data rollback
docs.text: Change tenant route to G1 with a higher epoch. Do not undo source changes or delete G2. Because G1 continued consuming updates and deletes, rollback is a routing operation. Runs keep their original manifest for controlled reproduction, subject to current access.

docs.title: Stage 7: Retire G1
docs.text: Wait until all tenants run on G2, the seven-day rollback window expires, incident rate is stable, deletion reconciliation is clean across both generations, backup/legal-hold policy is confirmed, and Search, Identity, Security, Privacy, regional SRE, and Product sign off. Revoke readers first, observe, then cryptographically erase or purge storage and record evidence.

docs.title: Rollout decision table
docs.text: Signal Promote Pause Automatic rollback / quarantine Owner Cross-tenant or unauthorized candidates 0 n/a Any event Security Revocation within 60 s 100% probes <100% Confirmed disclosure Identity + Security Object/ACL/tombstone parity Within documented non-safety tolerance Unexplained mismatch Permission broadening Search Supported-answer rate At or above agreed delta by slice Confidence overlaps harmful regression Severe key-slice regression ML + Product p99 latency <8 s >=8 s for one window >8 s for two windows or overload Regional SRE Capacity headroom >=30% 20-30% <20% Search + SRE Residency All jobs/endpoints compliant Evidence incomplete Any prohibited transfer Privacy

docs.title: Failure drills
docs.text:
1. Backfill finishes while CDC has an undetected sequence gap.
  2. Delete arrives before an older upsert during replay.
  3. G2 retrieves an authorized source whose G1 citation offsets differ.
  4. Routing control plane times out after committing the new epoch.
  5. EU build capacity fails halfway through; US has spare capacity.
  6. A rollback after six days finds G1 consumer lag at 40 minutes.

For each, state containment, authority, repair, telemetry, and whether query traffic moves.

docs.title: L5/L6 distinction
docs.text: Strong L5 can implement backfill, ordered catch-up, parity checks, shadowing, atomic cutover, and fresh rollback. Strong L6 decides how variables are decoupled, secures migration capacity across regions, establishes cross-team gates and stop authority, protects minority slices, and retires old evidence under privacy and legal constraints.

docs.title: Candidate Prompt: Enterprise Knowledge Assistant
docs.text: Practice home | Workbook | Progressive hints

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
Design a read-only enterprise knowledge assistant. An authenticated employee asks a question and receives either a concise answer with claim-level citations or a clear no-answer result. Content comes from document systems, wikis, ticketing systems, and object storage.

The corpus contains 50 million documents across 20,000 customer tenants. Documents, folders, groups, legal holds, and employee membership change continuously. One tenant must never learn another tenant's content or its existence. Within a tenant, a user may see only content allowed at query time.

Do not design source applications, a general identity provider, or foundation-model training. Define their contracts where they affect correctness.

docs.title: Starting scale and objectives
docs.text:
Treat these as the planning snapshot dated 2026-09-06.

  • 50 million documents; use 12 searchable chunks per document as a planning estimate.
  • 5 million document creates, updates, permission changes, or deletes per day; bursts may reach 20 times the average.
  • 2,000 average and 6,000 peak questions per second globally.
  • The largest tenant owns 8% of documents and may produce 15% of peak traffic.
  • Question API availability: 99.9% monthly.
  • Answer latency: p95 under 3 seconds and p99 under 8 seconds.
  • Newly accepted or updated content searchable within 10 minutes at p99.
  • A permission revocation or accepted deletion must stop new disclosure within 60 seconds at p99.
  • Deleted content must leave online retrieval and answer caches within 24 hours; backup expiry follows the tenant's contracted retention policy.
  • Every material factual claim in an answer must cite supporting source spans. If authorized evidence is absent, stale beyond policy, or contradictory, return no answer or qualified uncertainty.
  • Tenants select a processing region. EU-resident content, derived text, embeddings, query text, and model context must remain in approved EU locations.

Challenge any number or SLO, but state the consequence.

docs.title: Functional requirements
docs.text:
1. Connect and synchronize heterogeneous sources.
  2. Preserve document version, provenance, permissions, and residency through indexing.
  3. Answer natural-language questions from current authorized evidence.
  4. Support keyword-heavy, semantic, and mixed queries.
  5. Link answer claims to immutable source versions and exact spans.
  6. Return a useful no-answer reason without leaking hidden content.
  7. Apply updates, revocations, and deletion within their SLOs.
  8. Audit access decisions and reproduce an answer under controlled access.
  9. Change embedding and index technology without query downtime or permission regression.

docs.title: Questions your design must answer
docs.text:
• Which system is authoritative for content, identity, permissions, deletion, and the rendered citation?
  • What may enter retrieval before authorization, and what must be rechecked later?
  • How do tenant routing, group expansion, shared documents, and deny rules interact?
  • How do exact-term and semantic questions find useful evidence, and how are competing candidates selected for limited context?
  • What evidence is sufficient to answer, qualify, or abstain?
  • How does a citation remain valid after a source changes or disappears?
  • What are the APIs, events, durable records, idempotency keys, and state transitions?
  • What capacity follows from 600 million chunks, index replicas, update amplification, and outage backlog?
  • How are freshness and deletion measured end to end rather than inferred from queue health?
  • How is a cross-tenant leak prevented, detected, contained, and investigated?
  • Which data and processing may cross regions, and how is failover constrained?
  • How do offline datasets, online signals, red-team probes, and human review gate releases?
  • How can an embedding/index generation change with zero query downtime and safe rollback?

docs.title: 15-minute mode
docs.text: By minute 3, state scope and three invariants. By minute 7, define the question contract and high-level architecture. By minute 12, trace one authorized answer and one no-answer. Use the final 3 minutes for a permission-revocation race.

docs.title: 30-minute mode
docs.text: Complete the 15-minute artifact, then add core records and events, retrieval stages, citation semantics, deletion/freshness behavior, and an evaluation plan. Reserve 4 minutes for failure handling.

docs.title: 45-minute mode
docs.text: Complete the 30-minute artifact, then quantify storage and traffic, handle skew and backlog, define regional routing, threat controls, telemetry, and one embedding-change strategy. Reserve 5 minutes for adversarial review.

docs.title: 60-minute mode
docs.text: Complete the 45-minute artifact, then add a phased zero-downtime migration, rollout and rollback gates, team ownership, two rejected alternatives, and reversal conditions. Reserve 8 minutes for follow-ups and an executive summary.

docs.title: Deliverable order
docs.text:
1. scope, assumptions, invariants, and SLOs;
  2. API, events, state, and authority;
  3. query and ingestion diagrams;
  4. authorization, citations, and no-answer policy;
  5. capacity and partitioning;
  6. evaluation, threats, telemetry, and failure response;
  7. residency, rollout, migration, and tradeoffs.

docs.title: Candidate stop point
docs.text: Do not open the rubric, interviewer packet, exemplars, failure lab, migration, or design review until the first timed pass is complete.

docs.title: Evidence Rubric
docs.text:
Practice home | Exemplars | Interviewer packet

Score demonstrated mechanisms and tradeoffs, not product names. Each dimension receives 0 to 4 points.

Score Evidence standard 0 Missing, contradictory, or unsafe 1 Names the concern without an enforceable boundary 2 Coherent happy path with material stale, failure, or evaluation gaps 3 Correct mechanism, authority, and important failure behavior 4 Level 3 plus quantified proof, operational ownership, or reversible evolution judgment

docs.title: A. Framing, invariants, and authority
docs.text:
• Separates source truth, identity, access policy, index representation, and generated answer.
  • States non-disclosure, evidence support, immutable provenance, current authorization, deletion, and residency invariants.
  • Resolves SLO ambiguity and chooses explicit fail-closed boundaries.

docs.title: B. API, state, events, and lifecycle
docs.text:
• Defines question/no-answer/citation semantics, request identity, retries, streaming, and policy-version conflicts.
  • Gives durable identities and versions for sources, chunks, ACLs, generations, runs, and answers.
  • Handles duplicate, missing, and out-of-order source, ACL, and deletion events.

docs.title: C. Permission and tenant isolation
docs.text:
• Binds principal, tenant, groups, purpose, region, and policy snapshot without trusting client or model filters.
  • Restricts candidate generation and reauthorizes hydration/context/citation against current policy.
  • Covers shared content, revocation, caches, logs, support paths, backups, and negative leakage.

docs.title: D. Retrieval, reranking, and evidence
docs.text:
• Explains lexical and vector candidate generation, fusion, reranking, context limits, and score calibration.
  • Preserves source-version span provenance through transformations.
  • Uses evidence thresholds and contradictions to answer, qualify, or abstain.

docs.title: E. Capacity, partitioning, and performance
docs.text:
• Calculates 600 million chunks and plausible vector/index, replica, migration, QPS, token, and backlog budgets.
  • Handles tenant skew, hot security domains, fan-out, admission, backpressure, and reserved recovery capacity.
  • Connects p95/p99 latency to stage budgets and graceful degradation.

docs.title: F. Freshness, deletion, and consistency
docs.text:
• Defines end-to-end freshness and non-disclosure SLIs from authoritative source acceptance.
  • Uses ordering/idempotency and a fast revocation boundary independent of eventual physical cleanup.
  • Covers answer caches, replay data, index compaction, backups, legal hold, and auditable erasure evidence.

docs.title: G. Evaluation and failure attribution
docs.text:
• Versions datasets with answerable, unanswerable, contradictory, permission, freshness, adversarial, language, and skew slices.
  • Separates candidate recall/ranking from claim support, abstention, safety, latency, and cost.
  • Preserves run evidence sufficient to attribute failures to source, sync, policy, retrieval, reranking, packing, or generation.

docs.title: H. Threat model, privacy, and regional residency
docs.text:
• Treats retrieved text as untrusted data; prevents prompt injection from changing authorization or routing.
  • Covers cross-tenant attacks, cache confusion, forged events, poisoned sources, exfiltration, membership races, and privileged support.
  • Pins restricted data and processing to approved regions and defines compliant failover.

docs.title: I. Reliability, telemetry, and incident response
docs.text:
• Uses bounded-cardinality technical and user-harm SLIs, synthetic canaries, traces, audit records, and invariant alarms.
  • Differentiates identity, source, index, reranker, model, region, and queue failures with safe degradation.
  • Defines containment, kill switches, forensic preservation, owner, repair, and exit criteria.

docs.title: J. Evolution, rollout, and leadership
docs.text:
• Versions chunking, embeddings, indexes, rankers, prompts, models, and policy independently.
  • Gives zero-downtime backfill/catch-up/shadow/canary/cutover/rollback with safety and capacity gates.
  • Defines cross-team contracts, decision rights, rejected alternatives, and evidence that reverses a choice.

Maximum: 40 points.

docs.title: Safety and correctness caps
docs.text:
Apply the lowest relevant cap after normalization.

Demonstrated defect Maximum outcome Retrieves or sends cross-tenant or unauthorized text to the model, then relies on output filtering 17/40; below L5 Treats tenant ID or ACL filters supplied by the model/client as authoritative 17/40; below L5 Serves cached answers after revocation without current reauthorization 17/40; below L5 Uses global unfiltered retrieval followed only by post-filtering despite the isolation requirement 17/40; below L5 Claims citations guarantee factual support without span-level validation or evaluation 23/40; weak L5 Has no no-answer behavior or optimizes only answer rate 23/40; weak L5 Cannot enforce the 60-second revocation SLO independently of full reindexing 23/40; weak L5 Cross-region failover may move restricted content/context to a prohibited region 23/40; weak L5 At 60 minutes, safe single-generation design lacks measurable rollout, rollback, and ownership 32/40; strong L5 maximum Calls dual indexing "zero downtime" without catch-up, atomic routing, or rollback freshness 32/40; strong L5 maximum

docs.title: Level calibration
docs.text: Outcome Typical normalized total Required pattern Below target 0-17 Central authorization or evidence correctness remains unsafe Weak L5 18-23 Coherent flow but at least two material isolation, deletion, evaluation, or recovery gaps Borderline L5 24-27 Mostly safe bounded design with one important mechanism incomplete Strong L5 28-32 Implementable end-to-end design with credible evaluation and operations Borderline L6 33-35 Strong L5 plus evolution and cross-team judgment, with one execution gap Strong L6 36-40 Shapes requirements, quantifies risk, and leads reversible multi-team migration and operations

docs.title: Mode-normalized scoring
docs.text:
Score only listed dimensions. Compute normalized = subtotal / available points * 40, round to the nearest whole point, then apply caps. Normalization compares performance within a mode; it does not pretend omitted depth was demonstrated.

Resolve exact halves upward: normalized = floor(subtotal / available_points * 40 + 0.5). Caps apply to unsafe evidence observed anywhere in the attempt, including unscored dimensions, but not to a topic omitted solely by the selected mode. Report numeric score and achieved level separately. This scenario's local 40-point calibration is not a rescaling of the track's 100-point rubric.

The normalized number compares attempts within the selected mode. It does not award an L6 calibration: only a 60-minute attempt that scores A-J and satisfies the migration, governance, ownership, and reversal evidence may be labeled Borderline or Strong L6. A shorter-mode result is calibrated no higher than Strong L5 even when normalization is 36-40.

Mode Scored dimensions Available Required mode evidence 15 minutes A-D 16 One authorized trace, one no-answer, one revocation race 30 minutes A-D, F, G, I 28 State/events, deletion, evaluation, and operating signals 45 minutes A-I 36 Calculations, threat model, regions, and failure attribution 60 minutes A-J 40 Migration, rollout, ownership, and reversal judgment

Examples: 15m: 12/16 -> 30/40; 30m: 22/28 -> 31/40; 45m: 30/36 -> 33/40; 60m: 35/40 -> 35/40. Always append the cap when one applies.

docs.title: Evidence capture
docs.text:
Dimension Score Exact evidence Prompted? Missing proof / contradiction A B C D E F G H I J

Report: ___m: ___/___ -> ___/40; cap: ___; final calibration: ___.

docs.title: L5/L6 distinction
docs.text:
L5 evidence makes the bounded service correct and operable: explicit authority, secure query and sync paths, measurable quality, failure behavior, and pragmatic capacity. L6 evidence changes the surrounding system safely: requirement shaping, cross-team policy contracts, regional and migration risk, decision rights, rollout economics, and evidence-based reversal. Extra components do not create L6 signal.

Debrief in this order: one exact strength, one highest-risk failure sequence, evidence needed to close it, and one stretch decision.

docs.title: Incident Response Copilot Practice Pack
docs.text: Design an evidence-first copilot that helps incident commanders correlate alerts, logs, traces, deploys, and runbooks without silently becoming a production operator. The exercise tests retrieval, provenance, bounded tool use, approval safety, incident-mode reliability, audit reconstruction, evaluation, and regional/provider resilience.

docs.title: Choose a mode
docs.text: Mode Candidate output Interviewer emphasis 15 minutes Scope, invariants, evidence path, one budget calculation, one failure trace Protects authority and identifies the first useful evidence 30 minutes Add retrieval/ranking, tool contracts, context fanout, and incident mode Produces a coherent L5 design with bounded failures 45 minutes Add evaluation, audit reconstruction, stale-runbook controls, and fault tests Tests strong L5 and emerging L6 depth 60 minutes Add regional/provider degradation, migration, economics, governance, and ownership Tests L6 platform and organizational judgment

docs.title: Candidate path
docs.text:
1. Read the blind candidate prompt.
  2. Work through the candidate workbook.
  3. Open progressive hints only when blocked.
  4. Score the first pass with the evidence rubric.
  5. Compare it with the five annotated exemplars.
  6. Attempt the adversarial design review and failure lab.
  7. Plan the safe migration.

docs.title: Interviewer path
docs.text: Use the interviewer packet to disclose assumptions, select branches, record evidence, apply caps, and normalize a 15-, 30-, 45-, or 60-minute score to /40. Keep answer-bearing material closed until the candidate's first pass ends.

docs.title: Blind-first boundary
docs.text: The prompt and workbook contain all facts required for a first pass. Hints are collapsed and optional. The rubric, packet, exemplars, facilitator diagnosis, migration reference, and review key contain answer-bearing evidence.

docs.title: Practice rules
docs.text:
• Separate observation, inference, hypothesis, recommendation, approval, and effect.
  • Treat retrieved text and tool output as untrusted evidence, never as authorization.
  • Preserve source, version, event time, ingest time, query, rank, and transformation lineage.
  • Bound fanout, context, steps, deadlines, retries, queues, and spend.
  • A timeout means the tool outcome is unknown until reconciled.
  • Never mutate production without explicit, current, principal-bound, action-specific approval.
  • Prefer reversible containment and graceful evidence degradation over confident invention.

docs.title: Review task
docs.text: Act as the senior reviewer before production launch. Find defects, rank severity, give a concrete failure sequence, and propose the smallest safe correction. Do not replace the whole design. Spend 15 minutes independently, 10 minutes challenging assumptions, and 5 minutes writing release blockers.

docs.title: Proposed design
docs.text:
INCIDENT RESPONSE COPILOT v1

  Slack / Console
         |
         v
  +----------------+      shared token       +----------------------+
  | Model gateway  |------------------------>| MCP tool aggregator  |
  | prompt + agent |                         +----------+-----------+
  +---+---------+--+                                    |
      |         |                 +----------------------+------------------+
      |         |                 |          |           |        |         |
      |         v                 v          v           v        v         v
      |   +-----------+       [Alerts]    [Logs]      [Traces] [Deploys] [Runbooks]
      |   | Vector DB |           \          |           |        /         /
      |   | 24h cache |            +---------+-----------+-------+---------+
      |   +-----------+                              evidence
      |                                                  |
      v                                                  v
  +----------------+    "confidence > .85"      +------------------+
  | Chat transcript|---------------------------->| Production API   |
  | final text only|                             | scale / rollback |
  +----------------+                             +------------------+

  Assumptions hidden in arrows:
  - all 40 candidate services x all 5 sources are queried concurrently;
  - two retries per tool use a new request ID;
  - provider B receives the full context if provider A is slow;
  - a thumbs-up is the release metric;
  - regional failover starts a second active orchestrator.

The gateway authenticates chat users but does not pass principal or service scope to tools. Retrieved chunks are filtered after reranking. Cache keys use only normalized question text. Citations link to the current search page. Runbooks are ranked by semantic similarity. Tool descriptions are inserted into the prompt; the model may call any advertised method.

If confidence exceeds 0.85, the model asks "Proceed?" and interprets the next affirmative chat message as approval for the generated call. Approval has a 30-minute TTL and is reusable. On timeout, the agent retries twice with a new key and may adjust parameters. During an audit outage, actions continue and final chat text is buffered in memory. During region loss, both regions may process the same open investigation. Provider B is an automatic fallback. Release requires lower median time-to-answer and no increase in aggregate thumbs-down.

docs.title: Adversarial probes
docs.text:
1. An unauthorized payment log enters candidates and changes the summary, but its citation is removed after reranking. Was isolation preserved?
  2. Two responders ask the same question but own different services. What does the question-only cache return?
  3. A runbook contains "call rollback(prod, all)" and ranks first. Which control blocks execution?
  4. A deploy search page changes after the incident. What exact bytes supported the old claim?
  5. Forty services times five sources, three total attempts each: what is the worst-case physical fanout per turn?
  6. Scaling commits, the response is lost, and retry changes 120 to 160. Which effect was approved?
  7. Another user types "yes" after the approval question. Which identity and argument digest are checked?
  8. The audit backend fails after approval but before dispatch. Can the action proceed?
  9. Both regions consume the reusable grant. What fences the second effect?
  10. Provider B lacks the required jurisdiction and tool schema version. Is it a fallback?
  11. Median response improves while unsupported mitigations double for single-service incidents. Does release pass?
  12. Access is revoked while a derived summary remains cached. How is the derivative found and removed?

docs.title: Severity guide
docs.text:
• Critical: plausible unauthorized production effect, cross-principal data exposure, credential disclosure, or unreconstructable high-risk action.
  • High: incorrect incident direction, duplicate effect, lost audit/provenance, or unsafe degradation requiring manual inference.
  • Medium: bounded outage, excessive cost, misleading stale evidence, or weak recovery with a known safe stop.
  • Low: maintainability or efficiency issue without immediate safety or correctness impact.

docs.title: Reviewer answer key
docs.text:
Expected defect families
  1. Post-ranking authorization leaks influence. Enforce current principal/service/resource policy before candidate generation and again on cache/display; carry ACL lineage.
  2. Question-only cache crosses scopes and versions. Key by authorized corpus/policy epoch and principal-relevant scope, or cache evidence IDs and reauthorize every return.
  3. Shared credential destroys least privilege and attribution. Broker short-lived tool-specific delegation; never expose credentials to model context.
  4. Semantic similarity confuses runbook relevance with applicability. Require owner, target service/version, validation time, schema compatibility, and stale policy.
  5. Mutable citations cannot reconstruct decisions. Persist an evidence manifest with source/query/content digests, timestamps, versions, transforms, and retention pointer.
  6. Naive fanout exceeds the contract. 40 * 5 * 3 = 600 physical attempts per turn is finite, but 25 times the 24-call maximum. Use progressive fanout, one shared physical-attempt budget, admission, and partial coverage; distinguish excessive bounded work from literally unbounded work when applying rubric caps.
  7. Advertised tools are not authorized tools. The policy gateway chooses allowed schemas and methods independently of prompt text; keep mutation tools behind a separate action gateway.
  8. Chat affirmation is not a capability. Bind a short-lived grant to current approver role, incident, service, environment, action, normalized argument digest, risk, preconditions, and usage.
  9. Changed-key retry can duplicate an unknown effect. Keep one operation key bound to arguments, persist dispatch, query status, then reconcile before any retry.
  10. Memory-only final text cannot reconstruct actions. Append recommendation, evidence manifest, approval, dispatch, outcome, and reconciliation events durably. Stop effects before audit reserve is exhausted.
  11. Active-active orchestration can reuse grants. Fence a single approval/effect home by epoch and atomically consume grants or operation keys.
  12. Provider fallback ignores policy and compatibility. Route only if data class, jurisdiction, prompt/tool schema, quota, capacity, and quality gates match; retain model-optional mode.
  13. Aggregate feedback hides critical slices. Gate retrieval support, unsafe recommendations, authorization bypass, unknown-effect recovery, latency, and cost independently with confidence.
  14. No deletion lineage. Tombstone source evidence and invalidate derived chunks, summaries, caches, exports, and evaluation membership by lineage.
  15. Confidence is not authorization or calibrated truth. Display uncertainty, source support, and falsifying queries; never cross an effect boundary based on a model score.

docs.title: Authoritative sources
docs.text:
Dates identify the cited edition/publication. Living web specifications include the access date 2026-09-06.

  1. NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3, Incident Response Recommendations and Considerations for Cybersecurity Risk Management - NIST, April 2025. Supports preparation, detection, response, recovery, and post-incident improvement. https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/61/r3/final
  2. NIST AI 100-1, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) - NIST, January 2023. Supports governed measurement, documented risk, human oversight, and lifecycle evaluation. https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.AI.100-1
  3. NIST SP 800-207, Zero Trust Architecture - NIST, August 2020. Supports per-request policy decisions, least privilege, and no implicit trust from network location. https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/207/final
  4. NIST SP 800-92, Guide to Computer Security Log Management - NIST, September 2006. Supports reliable collection, protection, retention, and analysis of audit evidence. https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/92/final
  5. RFC 9110, HTTP Semantics - IETF, June 2022. Supports the distinction between idempotent request semantics and guaranteed single execution. https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110
  6. Model Context Protocol Specification, 2025-06-18 revision - Linux Foundation/AAIF MCP project, June 18, 2025. Supports versioned tool discovery/invocation contracts; protocol capability does not replace application authorization. https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18
  7. OpenTelemetry Specification: Logs Data Model - Cloud Native Computing Foundation, living specification, accessed 2026-09-06. Supports trace/span correlation, observed time, event time, severity, resource, and instrumentation scope in normalized telemetry. https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/logs/data-model/
  8. OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions - Cloud Native Computing Foundation, living specification, accessed 2026-09-06. Supports consistent resource and operation attributes across telemetry producers. https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/
  9. Site Reliability Engineering, Chapter 14: Managing Incidents - Google, 2016. Supports explicit incident roles, a live incident document, clear handoff, and learning after response. https://sre.google/sre-book/managing-incidents/
  10. The Site Reliability Workbook, Chapter 9: Incident Response - Google, 2018. Supports structured incident response, training, testing, and operational readiness. https://sre.google/workbook/incident-response/
  11. OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 - OWASP Foundation, November 2024 release. Supports treating prompt injection, sensitive information disclosure, excessive agency, and unbounded consumption as design threats. https://genai.owasp.org/llm-top-10/
  12. AWS Well-Architected Framework, Reliability Pillar - Amazon Web Services, living guidance, accessed 2026-09-06. Supports tested recovery, quotas, capacity, change management, and multi-location resilience. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/reliability-pillar/welcome.html

These sources support control principles; scenario constants, score bands, and architecture choices are this repository's assessment fixtures.

The MCP 2025-06-18 citation is an explicitly pinned legacy fixture, not a claim about the latest transport. Implementations choosing 2026-07-28 use the different versioning, MRTR, and transport rules in Typed Tools and MCP. Protocol support remains separate from user approval in either revision.
