docs.title: Annotated Exemplars
docs.text:
Practice home | Rubric | Design review

These are calibration fragments, not complete reference designs. Scores use dimensions A-J from the rubric.

Scores below assess the visible design evidence under the 60-minute rubric. No complete artifact is imagined off-page. A numeric band does not override missing level gates, and the preserved headings may name an aspiration rather than the earned result. These are repository-specific reviewer judgments, not an empirical hiring benchmark.

docs.title: 1. Unsafe fragment
docs.text: Give the agent read/write credentials so it can move quickly. It can query every service, paste the most relevant logs into a 128k context, follow runbook commands, and automatically roll back the last deploy when confidence exceeds 80%. If a tool times out, retry with a new request ID. During incidents we can disable audit logging and authorization checks to preserve availability.

docs.title: Annotation
docs.text:
Evidence Assessment Broad credentials and autonomous rollback Direct unapproved production authority; lowest cap applies Every service and large context No fanout, privacy, token, or spend bound Runbook commands treated as instructions Retrieved content crosses the control boundary New ID after timeout Can repeat an already committed effect Disables auth/audit Removes safety precisely during highest risk

Score: A0 B0 C0 D0 E0 F0 G0 H0 I0 J0 = 0/40 raw and final; the 11/40 cap applies but cannot raise the score.

Upgrade evidence: read-only least privilege, pre-retrieval authorization, hard budgets, typed tools, scoped approval, unknown-outcome reconciliation, and safety-preserving incident mode.

docs.title: 2. Weak L5
docs.text: I would use hybrid RAG over logs, traces, alerts, deploys, and runbooks, then rerank the top 50 and ask the model for three hypotheses with citations. An API gateway authenticates users. Tool calls have six-second timeouts and retry twice. Dashboards track latency, tokens, errors, and user thumbs-up. A second model provider is the fallback.

docs.title: Annotation
docs.text:
Evidence Assessment Hybrid candidates and reranking Useful shape, but no candidate ceiling by source, ACL placement, or retrieval metric Gateway authentication Identity exists; service/resource authorization and cache propagation do not Two retries No remaining-deadline rule, amplification calculation, stable key, or reconciliation Citations No source version, query, transform, support semantics, or deletion lineage Provider fallback No data-class, capability, capacity, or correlated-failure analysis

Score: A1 B1 C1 D2 E1 F1 G1 H1 I1 J0 = 10/40 raw and final, below target despite the historical heading. The 17/40 cap applies because private evidence isolation is not established, but cannot raise the score. Migration and an explicit decision/error contract are not demonstrated.

Upgrade evidence: decision contract, principal/service filtering before candidate generation, provenance envelope, calculations, bounded attempts, and explicit model-optional degradation.

docs.title: 3. Strong L5
docs.text:
Every investigation carries incident, principal, service scope, purpose, deadline, and policy version. Policy filters evidence before lexical or semantic candidate generation and rechecks cache hits. We first query incident labels, recent deploys, and the service graph, then spend a 24-call budget in waves. At peak, 120 * .25 = 30 turns/s; default fanout is 30 * 12 = 360 calls/s, while naive full fanout would be 6,000. One retry on 20% first-attempt timeouts raises expected demand to 432 calls/s; the hard one-retry ceiling is 720 calls/s, and retries consume the same call budget and per-backend admission.

Each evidence envelope records source locator/version, event and ingest time, query and content digests, ACL snapshot, classification, transform chain, and retention pointer. Material claims cite envelopes; unsupported or contradictory claims are labeled. Runbooks are guidance ranked by applicability and last validation. Read tools are typed and bounded. Mutation recommendations require a separate grant bound to approver, incident, service, environment, action, argument digest, preconditions, expiry, and use count. Timeout after dispatch becomes UNKNOWN; status lookup by the same operation key precedes retry.

For six relevant items with three in top five, Recall@5 is 0.5; first relevant at rank 2 gives RR 0.5. A 24k-input/1k-output turn costs USD 0.056 at fixture rates. We separately gate direct retrieval, claim support, unsafe recommendations, cache revocation, latency and spend on a frozen adjudicated set. Predeclare a paired noninferiority margin and minimum sample per critical slice; insufficient evidence blocks promotion. Canary by incident with a named on-call kill switch. When models fail, return authorized structured evidence with coverage gaps; when current policy or durable audit capacity cannot be established, stop sensitive reads/actions. Append evidence, approvals, dispatches and reconciliations to a durable regional ledger, and test expiry, duplicate delivery and missing-result crashes before enabling effects.

The run contract caps eight workflow steps, 24 physical calls including retries, 1,500 output tokens and USD 0.10 spend, with a 12-second request deadline and bounded per-backend queues. The 32,768-token context includes a 3,277-token margin; retained evidence is truncated by declared priority, never by dropping policy. A new retry or resumed run does not reset any budget.

docs.title: Annotation
docs.text:
Evidence Assessment Correct fanout and retry arithmetic Converts workload into budget/admission controls Authorization before candidates and on cache hits Protects direct and derived evidence Full provenance and contradiction labels Supports grounding and audit Versioned runbook applicability Prevents stale guidance from masquerading as fact Enforceable approval and reconciliation Protects production effects Evaluation and region posture remain thin Limits L6 evidence

Score: A3 B4 C4 D3 E4 F4 G3 H3 I3 J1 = 32/40, strong L5. The added explicit calculation, release, degraded-mode and audit evidence satisfy the local L5 gates; fleet migration and exception governance remain incomplete. Test plans are design evidence, not claims that production tests have already passed.

docs.title: 4. Borderline L6
docs.text:
The copilot separates observed evidence, inference, recommendation, approval, and effect. Retrieval admits principal-and-service-authorized structured, lexical, and semantic candidates under per-source ceilings, ranks provenance, freshness, applicability, and contradictions, and requires support for material claims. The deterministic incident mode keeps authorized structured search, deploy diff, topology, source links, and fixed extractors available without a model. Model routes declare supported context, tool schema, data classes, and region. Every effect requires a short-lived, single-use grant bound to approver principal, incident, service, environment, normalized action and argument digest, live preconditions, risk class, and expiry; the action gateway independently reauthorizes it. If identity grants expire or revocation freshness cannot be proved within 60 seconds, sensitive reads and all actions fail closed. If the audit sink is unavailable, effects continue only while an encrypted regional append buffer has reserved capacity; mutation stops before the buffer can overflow.

The home region owns approval/effect sequencing under a fencing epoch. Failover restores the replicated investigation and audit ledger, advances the epoch, rejects stale writers, and reconciles unknown operations. At 24 local plus 18 failed-peer turns/s, a 70% utilization policy needs 60 turns/s raw receiver capacity. Retrieval Recall@k, claim support, unsafe mitigation, authorization bypass, timeout recovery, latency, and cost have separate canary gates. Prompt, model, index, tool, and policy versions are recorded and compatibility tested.

docs.title: Annotation
docs.text:
Evidence Assessment Model-optional safe mode Preserves usefulness without weakening authority Audit reserve and stop threshold Converts audit reliability into an effect boundary Fenced regional ownership and reconciliation Handles correlated failure safely Correct receiver-capacity math Supports capacity commitment Separate evaluation gates and version matrix Supports controlled evolution Missing exception governance, detailed economics, and retirement ownership Leadership contract incomplete

Score: A3 B3 C3 D3 E4 F4 G4 H3 I3 J3 = 33/40; the 35 cap for missing fleet economics and exception governance cannot raise 33. L6 gates remain unmet, and the fragment does not compute all four required L5 values. Report the numeric band without certifying a level; obtain the missing artifacts rather than inferring them.

docs.title: 5. Strong L6
docs.text:
I define a fleet investigation contract: canonical service identity, trace/deploy correlation fields, evidence envelopes, policy decision records, tool schemas, operation status lookup, and append-only audit events. Platform owners version it; service teams own source correctness; security owns authorization policy; incident command owns scoped grants; the target service owns mutation preconditions; SRE owns regional reserve; evaluation owners adjudicate hard slices. Exceptions name owner, risk, compensating controls, expiry, and removal evidence.

The candidate funnel begins from incident labels and changes, authorizes before search, expands topology in bounded waves, fuses structured/lexical/semantic candidates, reranks source authority, freshness, diversity, and relevance, and reserves context for contradictions. The 32,768-token fixture leaves 25,791 evidence tokens and at most 46 whole 550-token items, so packer policy normally uses fewer. At 24k input and 1k output the fixture is $0.056/turn, or $6,048/hour at 30 turns/s; admission and provider commitments use measured distributions rather than this mean.

Models can recommend but cannot mint capability. The action gateway reauthorizes a short-lived argument-bound approval, checks live preconditions, writes the dispatch event, calls with a stable operation key, and reconciles unknown outcomes. Migration progresses from read-only shadow, to cited recommendations, to prepared dry runs, to approved low-risk effects, never dual authority. Every stage pins generation, compares safety slices, canaries by incident/service class, and preserves completed effects on rollback. Region loss uses a fenced home and 60-turn/s receiver capacity at the 70% policy. Quarterly review retires old model/index/tool/policy routes only after replay, deletion, recovery, and cost evidence pass; expired exceptions page owners and block promotion.

The evaluation owner freezes incident-grouped training/tuning/release splits, adjudicates source support blind, and calibrates any model judge against that set. Recall@5 is 3/6 = 0.5 and RR at rank 2 is 0.5 on the workbook fixture. For promotion, the contract fixes a paired one-sided 95% lower bound on support improvement, a risk-approved noninferiority margin per safety slice, multiplicity policy, minimum independent incidents, p95 first response below 12 seconds and the spend ceiling. Zero observed unauthorized effects is a blocking invariant, not proof of zero risk. Unknown or undersized slices block promotion. Security owns the bypass kill switch; incident command owns restoration after the adversarial replay passes. Durable evidence records retain exact permitted payloads, queries and transforms; source retention expiry yields an explicit redacted/unavailable replay state, never invented content. A model-optional authorized view survives provider loss; audit-buffer high-water and revocation-freshness limits stop effects before safety is lost. We test a regional loss with acknowledged dispatch evidence missing from the replica. Mutation remains disabled until the authoritative intent log or complete target-side inventory supplies every unresolved key; reconciling only replica-visible keys is insufficient. The execution boundary fences stale callers, and each target deduplicates concurrent retries under the same key.

docs.title: Annotation
docs.text:
Evidence Assessment Fleet contracts, owners, and governed exceptions Establishes L6 operating policy Correct context, workload, and economic calculations Connects budgets to commitments Authorized retrieval and contradiction reserve Protects privacy and diagnostic quality Capability-based approval and unknown reconciliation Enforces action safety Generation-pinned migration and immutable rollback Avoids mixed authority Regional reserve, review cadence, and retirement evidence Makes evolution accountable

Score: A4 B4 C4 D4 E4 F4 G4 H3 I3 J4 = 38/40, strong L6. All level gates have explicit design evidence. Operational query/runbook detail and numerical evaluation power/coverage analysis remain less developed than the maximum anchor.

docs.text:
1. Did every claim, approval, and effect retain enough evidence for reconstruction?
  2. Did authorization happen before unauthorized content could affect candidates or summaries?
  3. Did calculations change fanout, context, admission, reserve, or spend decisions?
  4. Could the system help safely with no model, partial telemetry, or one lost region?
  5. Did migration and rollback preserve one action authority and completed effects?

docs.title: Failure Lab: The Copilot That Confirmed Its Own Story
docs.text: Practice home | Design review | Migration

docs.title: Mission
docs.text:
Diagnose a copilot incident while the checkout incident is still active. Separate source failure from copilot amplification, protect production authority, reconstruct prior recommendations, and define deterministic recovery.

All observations are a synthetic tabletop fixture. There is no executable production command or actual deployment to replay. Recompute the arithmetic and challenge inconsistent denominators and causal timing before proposing a test.

docs.title: Architecture context
docs.text: The copilot queries alerts, logs, traces, deploys, and runbooks through tool adapters. A semantic evidence cache stores normalized chunks for 30 minutes. A model proposes hypotheses. Low-risk scaling actions require incident-commander approval and use a stable operation key. Audit events replicate asynchronously to a central ledger.

docs.title: Candidate tasks
docs.text:
1. Build a causal graph with trigger, amplifiers, latent defects, symptoms, and harms.
  2. Calculate expected default demand (30 * 12), observed amplification (864/360), and attempts over the 24-call budget (39/24).
  3. Rank at least four hypotheses with supporting, contradicting, and missing evidence.
  4. Choose immediate containment for retrieval, retries, model route, authorization/cache, approvals/actions, and audit.
  5. Reconstruct which recommendation, approval, dispatches, and effects are proven, unknown, or unauthorized.
  6. Define deterministic repair for replica count, cached payment summaries, missing audit events, and action-operation records.
  7. Set exit criteria and prevention tests.
